newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold ends down on higher arrivals.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold ends down on higher arrivals.

text.p: ** Gold 24 carat closed 35 rupees lower at 4,670 rupees per 10 gramme against the previous close of 4,705 rupees on higher arrivals while subdued sentiments in the world market prompted fresh offerings. Gold was down by 35 rupees per 10 gramme on Wednesday.
** Prices of gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 500 rupees lower at 54,600 rupees per piece after losing 300 rupees on Wednesday.
** Silver (.999) closed 30 rupees lower at 6,810 rupees per kg against the previous close of 6,840 rupees amid sluggish industrial demand coupled with fresh unloading by stockists.

Gold 24 carat closed 35 rupees lower at 4,670 rupees per 10 gramme against the previous close of 4,705 rupees as fresh arrivals of the smuggled gold dragged prices lower while physical buying was at a low ebb, dealer said.
Gold was down by 35 rupees per 10 gramme on Wednesday.
"Arrivals of smuggled gold by sea have increased in the current week ahead of the monsoon," one broker said.
"Fear that local authorities may take preventive action also prompted panic selling among the traders," he said.

Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 500 rupees lower at 54,600 rupees per piece after losing 300 rupees on Wednesday. A drop in the licence premium to import gold also subdued market sentiment. The premium special gold import license dropped to 11.40/11.50 percent from 13/13.25 percent.

Silver (.999) closed 30 rupees lower at 6,810 rupees per kg against the previous close of 6,840 rupees as a subdued trend in the world market prompted fresh offerings while industrial buying remained at a low ebb. ($1=35.78 rupees)
